key_insight: Combined computational and neural-network modelling identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports rapid process-window mapping to reduce weld defects and stabilize thermal and axial-force responses in HDPE joining.
method: Simulate temperature, force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Combine model predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: The experimentally validated models achieved ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to about 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy beyond the tested process-parameter range is not established; new operating conditions require experimental validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
